description:
John Frank Stevens engineered one of the greatest engineering wonders of the world, the Panama Canal, but he had to overcome many challenges along the way. See more in this clip from Season 1, "The Panama Canal."

Watch all new episodes of The Engineering That Built the World, Sundays at 9/8c, and stay up to date on all of your favorite The HISTORY Channel shows at history.com/schedule. 

#HISTORY #EngineeringThatBuiltTheWorld

As the latest instillation of The HISTORY Channel’s popular “That Built” franchise, Engineering That Built the World sheds light on the iconic structures and engineering feats that have shaped and defined our nation and our world. From the Golden Gate Bridge, to the Panama Canal, Transcontinental Railroad, Statue of Liberty and beyond, this series tells the stories of the brilliant visionaries behind the most epic builds of the past two centuries. Up against insurmountable challenges, these are the unknown tales of rivalries, egos, backdoor politics and the brilliant engineering innovations that made the future possible.

comments.text:
Yes the engineers came up with the magnificent plan however none of those men actually built it. 
Come on History, if we are going to tell it then we should tell it all like how the contributors were treated; 
The Gold Roll: Exclusively for white Americans who were engineers, doctors, and foremen. 
They were paid in U.S. Gold coins, got paid sick leave, 42 days of vacation, and lived in luxury housing with plumbing and electricity.  
The Silver Roll: Consisted of over 30,000 workers, mostly from the West Indies (Barbados and Jamaica). 
They were paid in Panamanian Silver Pesos, which were worth exactly half the value of U.S. gold. 
They got zero paid leave and lived in overcrowded barracks or shacks.
